It's time, Canterbury | Te Hapū o Ngāti Wheke

The area around Rāpaki Marae, nestled in the beautiful Whakaraupō/Lyttelton Harbour, was once known for its great abundance of kaimoana. Climate change, pollution and deforestation have put that at risk, but a massive amount of community mahi is helping to turn the tide.

Te Hapū o Ngāti Wheke told us their story of how climate change has impacted mahinga kai around Rāpaki, and how the community is working together to restore their local environment.

Cook Islands Language Week 2023: Tuki Tuki Teni Teni - reviving a Cook Islands tradition

oin Tauraki Rongo as he takes us on a journey through a cherished Cook Islands children's game that has stood the test of time. 🌺🏞️ 

To the rhythmic beat of the chant, the coconut shell passes from hand to hand – a delightful test of wit and agility! 🙌🤹‍♂️ Watch as the laughter flows and friendships deepen, all in the spirit of joyous camaraderie. 🤗💃🎉 Embrace the cultural diversity as each dialect weaves its unique version of this beloved game. Let's keep these traditions alive! 🌸🗣️ 

#TukiTukiTeniTeni #CookIslandsTradition #CookIslandsLanguageWeek #ChildrensGames #CulturalHeritage #PlayAndLaugh #PreservingOurRoots 🥥🌊#CookIslandsLanguageWeek

Cook Islands Langage Week: Embrace the wisdom of the Cook Islands Pe'e chant!

This poignant Pe'e, passed from fathers to sons on special occasions, resonates with timeless guidance. 📜💙

Keutekarakia Mataroa, Cook Islands Consulate General, shares this cherished chant to inspire us all! 

Let these meaningful words speak to all of us, uniting our hearts with our ancestral language and heritage. 🏝️🗣️ Let the wisdom within connect us to our homeland and strengthen our cultural bond. 🌸🌐

🎶🙌 #CookIslandsLanguageWeek #PeEChant #CulturalWisdom #LanguageAndHeritage #ProudOfMyRoots #PacificHeritage 🌺#CookIslandsLanguageWeek

Resources and calendar of events found right here:
https://www.mpp.govt.nz/programmes/pacific-language-weeks/cook-islands-language-week/

Cook Islands Language Week: Poe Tiare Oki Koe Noku, a melody of love and farewell

Join Elizabeth Rakoia & Keutekarakia Mataroa Jnr (Aka KJ) as they serenade us with this heartfelt Cook Islands classic. 🎵🌸 🌺🎶 A Melody of Love and Farewell: Poe Tiare Oki Koe Noku💕 

This beautiful song is a testament to the cherished bonds we hold with our family and loved ones – a gentle reminder that distance may separate us, but our hearts remain intertwined forever. 💞

Follow Elizabeth Rakoia on our Instagram and Facebook Story throughout this amazing week of celebrations!

🏝️Happy Cook Island Language Week 2023 🌺💌 #PoeTiareOkiKoeNoku #CookIslandsLanguageWeek #FarewellMelody #CherishedConnections #PacificHeritage #FamilyForever 🤗🎶

Cook Islands Language Week Recipe of the Day: Poi Meika, the Cook Islands Banana Smoothie!

Watch as Mama Tangi guides us through this quick and easy recipe, passed down through generations. 

🍌🌴🥥Poi Meika, the Cook Islands Banana Smoothie! ✨ 
Simply mash a ripe banana and blend in the rich coconut cream – a delicious tropical delight that brings the Cook Islands right to your home! 🏝️😍🍹 Whether it's a sunny morning or a relaxing afternoon, enjoy this refreshing smoothie any day of the week! 🌞💚 

#PoiMeika #CookIslandsFlavours #TropicalDelight #CookIslandsHeritage #SmoothieLovers #CookIslandsLanguageWeek 🍌🌺🥥

Cook Island Language Week Song of the Day: "E Kaute" (Hibiscus) – an easy-to-learn melody

Join Mama Tangi and the Pa Metua Super Gold Club as they share the vibrant spirit of the Cook Islands through the beautiful song "E Kaute" (Hibiscus) – an easy-to-learn melody that will fill your heart with joy! 🌺💃🏽 

🌺🎶 Celebrating Cook Island Language Week 2023! 🇨🇰✨

Richard Edmundson - History Homecoming

Richard (Dick) Edmundson is a secondary school principal working in schools for them to be desirable places for all to learn and work. Reconnecting school and community, he is currently Principal of Ōhautahi Christchurch’s Te Aratai College (formerly Linwood College). Emphasising whanaungatanga, Learning-focussed relationships with students, whānau, staff and the wider community, from social agencies to businesses, define his practice as a school leader. His career includes Principal of Hornby High School and Assistant Principal at Aranui High School.

Andrew Hampton - History Homecoming

Andrew Hampton is Director-General of Security | Te Tumu Whakarae mō Te Pā Whakamarumaru. Before joining the New Zealand Security Intelligence Service, Andrew was Director-General of the Government Communications and Security Bureau (GCSB) for seven years. Andrew’s previous roles in the justice sector include Director of the Office of Treaty Settlements, Deputy Secretary for Courts, and Deputy Chief Executive at the Crown Law Office. He was also Deputy Secretary and Director of the Secretary’s Office at the Ministry of Education and the first Government Chief Talent Officer at the Public Service Commission.

Dr Marguerite Foxon - History Homecoming

Dr Marguerite Foxon is a performance improvement specialist with 30+ years of experience in managing small and large-scale evaluations for corporate, government and non-profit organisations. Her career has included several years as National Director of Education for Price Waterhouse Coopers in Australia, followed by 13 years in the US with Motorola as the Global Manager for Leadership Development and Evaluation. She has co-authored three books in her field and has written numerous articles.

Dr Vincent O'Malley - History Homecoming

Dr Vincent O’Malley, FRHistS MRSNZ, is an award-winning and bestselling historian who has written and published extensively on the history of Māori and Pākehā relations in nineteenth century Aotearoa New Zealand. In 2022, Voices from the New Zealand Wars won the general non-fiction category at the Ockham New Zealand Book Awards, and Vincent won the Prime Minister’s Award for Literary Achievement in Non-Fiction. This year he was a semi-finalist for the Kiwibank New Zealander of the Year. Vincent is a founding partner of HistoryWorks, a Wellington-based research consultancy specialising in Treaty of Waitangi research.

Matt Frost - History Homecoming

Matt Frost, QSM, is a Principal Advisor in Whaikaha – the first Ministry of Disabled People in the world. He was previously at the Ministry of Education as a Principal Advisor: Lived Experience. On human rights for disabled people, Matt has represented Aotearoa New Zealand at the UN in New York. His longstanding advocacy has included chairing the Implementation Advisory Group for the New Zealand Autism Spectrum Disorder Guideline and serving as Deputy Chair of the Living Guideline Group.
